messages:
incident_bot: Pager: Sev2 - increased 5xx and GPU OOMs observed on inference cluster eu-west-1. Metric: /v1/generate 5xx rate 18% over 5m. Customers: prioritized enterprise tenants. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/serving-runtime-oom.

sre_jade: saw the spike ~10:04 UTC. tail logs show repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` then container crashloop on node g-inf-12. Pods keep restarting rather than draining.

oncall_matt: I'm on it. starting live RCA. tagging @eng_runtime_lee for kernel/driver flags.

eng_runtime_lee: looking. initial suspicion: autoscaler oscillation causing rapid pod churn, KV-cache thrashing, large sequence workloads triggering heavier memory. Can you share the autoscaler events?

sre_jade: grabbing events now: ```kubectl get hpa -n inference --show-events
NAME         REFERENCE            TARGETS   MIN   MAX   AGE
model-a-hpa  Deployment/model-a    120%/80%    20    300   3h
... events: scaled from 24 -> 180 at 09:59, scaled down 180 -> 12 at 10:03 (scaleDownWindow 30s)```

ops_miguel: that downscale at 10:03 coincides with many pods being scheduled into saturated hosts, kernel OOMs on node g-inf-12 reported. Node flapped and kubelet restarted.

oncall_matt: temporary mitigation options: 1) pause autoscaler, 2) cordon noisy nodes, 3) enact a soft cap on eviction to reduce pod churn. Which do we want first?

sre_jade: pause autoscaler for the group and pin replicas to current steady safe count (set deployment replicas=100). Doing that now.```kubectl scale deploy model-a --replicas=100 -n inference```

support_ana: inbound tickets from 3 enterprise customers, one reporting "model responses failing with 502s" — flagged priority. Notified account teams.

eng_runtime_lee: while autoscaler is paused, we should reduce batch sizes and disable large-sequence jobs. Pushing temporary config: ```PATCH /configs/model-a
{"batch_max_tokens":512, "max_seq":1024, "quantize":false}``` — applying conservative runtime settings.

ops_miguel: cordoning g-inf-12 and g-inf-13. ```kubectl cordon g-inf-12 && kubectl cordon g-inf-13```; scheduling new pods away while we let kernel issues heal.

sre_jade: node logs: `kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 23456 (inference_worker) total-vm:14500000kB` and `nvidia-driver: GPU reset due to illegal address` — looks like a mixture of host OOM + GPU error.

oncall_matt: we have an immediate brownout on some customers — degraded but still mostly serving. Escalating to sev1 if error rates don't drop in 10m.

incident_bot: Update: error rate decreased to 6% after scale pause and node cordon (10:12 UTC). Continuing mitigation.

eng_runtime_lee: next steps: 1) roll a small driver restart on affected nodes during a quiet window, 2) add admission pod anti-affinity to avoid packing heavy pods on single host, 3) revisit autoscaler settings: increase cooldowns and add rate-limiting. Proposed autoscaler snippet: ```
minReplicas: 20
maxReplicas: 300
scaleUp:
  stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
scaleDown:
  stabilizationWindowSeconds: 600
  policies:
    - type: Percent
      value: 20
      periodSeconds: 60
```

sre_jade: applied anti-affinity override and bumped scaleDown window to 600s on the runtime autoscaler controller. Observed pod restarts drop to baseline after the change.

support_ana: customers updated: 3 acknowledged, two want root-cause timeline. Logged post-incident status updates to billing-critical channels.

ops_miguel: performed GPU driver soft-reload on g-inf-12,13 during controlled window. Verified `nvidia-smi` shows no persistent ECC errors.

oncall_matt: handing off to daytime oncall @sre_jade at 10:30 UTC. I'll monitor artifacts for 1h and then move to watch. :white_check_mark:

incident_bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> partial service restored. Keep monitoring for 2h.

sre_jade: filing follow-up: create postmortem, include timeline, autoscaler tuning, test for node OOM under load, action items: add anomaly alert for rapid scale deltas (>50% change in 5m), run kernel + driver stress test, and create a rollbackable autoscaler config change process. Assign to eng_runtime_lee and ops_miguel.

eng_runtime_lee: noted. will prepare driver/oom regression tests and a safe scaling playbook.

support_ana: client comms draft ready for review. will send to account teams once we have final RC.

oncall_matt: closing slack thread for live mitigation. moving to post-incident channel for write-up. thumbs up :+1:

incident_bot: Thread closed for live operations at 10:50 UTC.
